fields.description:
Add plan-review criterion T15 "overlay-derisk" so plans prove risky runtime mechanisms via a fast out-of-loop experiment BEFORE committing them into a slow, codified delivery loop (CI/CD, IaC apply, provisioning pipeline). Motivation: on infra epics, basic failures (a service that won't boot, a credential that doesn't authorize, a dependency that won't connect, a readiness check that never passes) are discovered only at the END of a long delivery cycle. No existing criterion rewards front-loading those checks into a cheap local run or a manual probe against the real target. This is a CORE built-in change (not project-specific), stack-agnostic (no hardcoded Terraform/docker), routed by the self-gating Pass-1 finder like the other Txx overlays.

## The finalized T15 rubric (design of record)

OVERLAY — apply only when ALL of the following hold; else PASS not-applicable.
- S1 Codified loop? the mechanism is delivered/validated by pushing through an automated pipeline or an environment/infrastructure apply, not by running or unit-testing code directly.
- S2 Slow or costly pass? one pass through that loop is slow (minutes-to-hours) or otherwise costly to run.
- S3 Runtime-only correctness? the change introduces behavior whose correctness only resolves when it actually runs in a realistic environment (boots, authenticates, connects, is authorized, passes readiness) — unreachable by static/unit checks.

When applicable, report a finding for each check not satisfied:
- (a) RISK NAMED — the plan identifies the specific mechanism(s) confirmable only by completing the full loop.
- (b) FAST OUT-OF-LOOP PROOF — for each named risk, the plan commits to proving it via the fastest feedback path available for that mechanism, outside the slow loop: running the unit locally/emulated where feasible, OR a manual experiment directly against the real target (an interactive call, a one-off CLI/console action, a probe script, a throwaway resource) where local reproduction isn't possible. The experiment is concrete and returns a verdict in minutes, not a delivery cycle. An unnamed "we'll verify" / "we'll check after deploy" does not satisfy it.
- (c) PROVE-THEN-CODIFY — the cheap experiment comes before committing the mechanism into the slow loop, so the loop validates an already-proven mechanism.
- (d) SCOPED CLEANUP — throwaway experiments are cleaned up afterward, with teardown that removes ONLY the artifacts the experiment itself created (the records a probe inserted, the scratch resource it spun up) and touches nothing pre-existing, shared, or persistent; a cleanup step that could delete, reset, or truncate a resource the experiment did not create (e.g. dropping an existing table or wiping a bucket to "reset" it) fails this check.

ANTI-FP: a manual experiment against the real target is a fully valid proof — never penalize choosing it over local reproduction; many stacks cannot be reproduced locally. A mechanism already proven elsewhere in the codebase needn't be re-proven.

Facet ~ empirical / approach-soundness; exec AGENT (it ground-checks that the named mechanism and named experiment are real/plausible against the codebase). Posture (advisory vs blocking) and block_threshold are NOT decided here — set by the normal registry/review process.

## Required companion change: T10 boundary partition
The de-risk (transient experiment) phase and T10's production-hardening phase must not overlap; there is no runtime cross-criterion suppression by design. Fix by partitioning in T10's own rubric text — add a scope clause: "This overlay evaluates the DURABLE infrastructure — the IaC/config that persists. Transient, throwaway experiments used to de-risk a mechanism before committing it — their creation, isolation, and teardown — are out of scope here." (T10 does NOT name T15 or any other overlay.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] all child tickets are closed
- [x] `rebar explain T15` renders the criterion with its descriptive name (not the bare id), and
      `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` regenerates
      `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` with a T15 section, with the criteria-guide and registry
      validators passing
- [x] the writing-a-passing-plan guide instructs authors to de-risk out-of-loop before slow delivery loops,
      evidenced by the T15 guidance appearing in `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md`
- [x] the coach-move decision (add or reject the proposed out-of-loop-proof move) is recorded on this epic
      as a comment naming the decision and its rationale
- [x] T10's rubric and regenerated criteria-guide section contain the scope clause partitioning durable infrastructure from transient de-risk experiments. Verify: `python -c "from pathlib import Path; phrase='This overlay evaluates the DURABLE infrastructure'; assert phrase in Path('src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T10.md').read_text(); assert phrase in Path('docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md').read_text()"` exits 0.
